subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.6 cron migration: jobs migrated from jobs.json have blank agent_id — scheduler silently skips them

question: Should legacy/defaulted cron jobs be repaired to persist the config-aware default agent id, or should OpenClaw keep blank `agent_id` rows and rely on runtime fallback until live upgrade proof confirms the skip?
rationale: The source gap is real, but choosing persistent migration behavior affects multi-agent upgrade compatibility and prior attempted fixes were closed unmerged.

options.title: Adopt config-aware migration
options.body: Repair doctor migration and create-time defaults to persist the configured default agent while preserving explicit agent ids, then require upgrade proof before close.

options.title: Keep runtime fallback only
options.body: Leave persisted `agent_id` blank for legacy rows and document/runtime-test that omitted ids are intentionally resolved at execution time.

options.title: Require live repro first
options.body: Hold implementation until a maintainer or contributor reproduces the v2026.5.28-to-current upgrade skip in a real or Crabbox setup.

recommendation.title: Adopt config-aware migration
recommendation.body: Repair doctor migration and create-time defaults to persist the configured default agent while preserving explicit agent ids, then require upgrade proof before close.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest history across cron SQLite persistence, legacy migration, and cron normalization files.
